before: Dealer position limits concern the largest exposure reached before a review horizon ends. A position can finish within its limit after crossing it earlier (Figure~\ref{fig:example}). We compare historical and conditional forecasts of this sampled absolute-position peak.

before: Historical headroom combines the current position with completed past peak behavior. Conditional models estimate additional relationships from finite historical windows. Matched histories and update schedules show whether the added conditioning improves the forecast.
after: Historical headroom combines the current magnitude with completed past peak behavior, while conditional models estimate additional relationships from finite historical windows. Matching histories and update schedules isolates the forecast gain associated with the added conditioning within each comparison.

after: The two official weekly reporting systems describe different aggregate exposures, so their comparisons retain separate reference procedures and source-specific scales.

after: Their chronological training, calibration and test design reports scores and coverage together, providing a natural comparison for the present forecasting task. Our peak response instead uses a complete future path segment and the current magnitude, producing different labels and limits.

after: Regression quantiles target asymmetric forecast errors directly \citep{koenker1978}, while autoregressive quantiles and quantile forests supply other conditioning structures \citep{engle2004,meinshausen2006}.

after: The target is the largest sampled absolute position from issue time through the stated horizon, with \(N_t\) denoting signed position and \(\mathcal F_t\) the issue-time information.
